alternatives.reason: The fragments may reveal what happens to leftover matter, but I will follow the ice first.

effect: The giant sent icy bodies inward along several possible paths, so I can follow one into warmer space.
reaction: The different possible paths make me curious about what happens to the ice.
reason: Following the icy bodies into warm space directly advances the first goal.
expectation: I expect some ice to vaporize as the bodies warm, though their final fate is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The bodies could also encounter the rocky worlds, but I want to follow their warming first.

reaction: The thin cloud trailing a small remnant is a striking detail.
reason: The icy bodies can cross the rocky worlds' orbits, so this may reveal another fate for them.
expectation: I expect some icy bodies to encounter the rocky worlds, although they may simply pass through the system.

alternatives.reason: The fragments crossing the giant's rings could address the other goal, but I want to follow the ice first.

effect: The icy bodies struck rocky worlds, completing the ice goal; leftover fragments are the remaining focus.
reaction: The uncertainty about how much water survives the impacts is interesting.
reason: The fragments cross the giant's rings, so this may show what becomes of some leftover matter.
expectation: I expect the fragments to collide with or alter the rings, though their exact fate is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The fragments could also be followed through warm space, but the ring encounter interests me first.

effect: The rocky fragments can strike the rings and eject icy spray; the only remaining combination follows fragments through warm space.
reaction: The spray makes the rings feel more dynamic.
reason: This is the only available combination and may show another fate for the leftover fragments.
expectation: I expect the fragments to produce dust or otherwise change in warm space, though their exact fate is uncertain.

effect: Collisions grind leftover stones into fine dust, which can now meet the material released from warming ice.
reaction: The two debris paths coming together is satisfying.
reason: This is the only available combination and follows both kinds of leftover material.
expectation: I expect the rocky dust and material from the ice to mix in warm space, though their final fate is uncertain.

effect: The rocky and icy debris mingle and scatter starlight, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The faint glow is a satisfying way to bring the two paths together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Bringing the two debris paths together into a faint glow gave the leftover matter a clear, connected outcome.

leastWorthwhile.text: Grinding the stones into dust was straightforward and less memorable on its own, although it set up the final combination.

surprise.text: I was struck by a small icy remnant trailing an immense, thin cloud as its ice turned directly to gas.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt notably arbitrary; the final two choices were the only available combinations, but their purposes were clear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the contrasting paths of ice and rocky debris, and their eventual convergence, made me curious about what else the system could reveal.
